<!doctype html>
<html lang="ko">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>어구독 예비고3 WEEK 01</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/orioncactus/pretendard@v1.3.9/dist/web/static/pretendard.min.css">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:wght@200;300;400;500;600&family=Source+Serif+4:ital,wght@0,400;0,600;0,700;1,400&family=Nanum+Pen+Script&family=Inter:wght@400;600;800&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<style>
@page { size: A4; margin: 0; }
* { box-sizing: border-box; }
html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; background: #fff; }
body { word-break: keep-all; overflow-wrap: break-word; font-family: Pretendard, sans-serif; color: #17181c; font-size: 9.2pt; line-height: 1.5; -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact; }
:root { --ink: #121a33; --navy: #1b2a57; --acc: #ff5a1f; --acc2: #ffb800; --hl: #ffe45c; --gray: #6a6d76; --rule: #d3d6dd; --cream: #fbf7ef; }
.page { width: 210mm; height: 297mm; padding: 12mm 14mm 15mm; position: relative; overflow: hidden; break-after: page; }
.page:last-child { break-after: auto; }
.en { font-family: Inter, Pretendard, sans-serif; font-size: 9.2pt; line-height: 1.62; letter-spacing: -0.005em; }
.disp { font-family: "Black Han Sans", Pretendard, sans-serif; font-weight: 400; }
.hl { background: linear-gradient(transparent 58%, var(--hl) 58%); }
.tip { font-family: "Nanum Pen Script", cursive; font-weight: 400; color: var(--acc); font-size: 15pt; line-height: 1.15; }
.tip b { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 7pt; letter-spacing: 0.12em; color: #fff; background: var(--acc); padding: 0.6mm 1.6mm; border-radius: 1mm; margin-right: 2mm; vertical-align: 1.5pt; }
/* running head */
.run { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 7.4pt; color: var(--gray); margin-bottom: 5mm; }
.run .brand { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); letter-spacing: 0.06em; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.run .brand i { font-style: normal; color: var(--acc); }
.foot { position: absolute; left: 14mm; right: 14mm; bottom: 8mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 7.2pt; color: var(--gray); }
.foot .pg { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); font-size: 9pt; }
/* part head */
.part { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: end; column-gap: 4mm; padding-bottom: 2.5mm; border-bottom: 2pt solid var(--ink); margin-bottom: 4mm; }
.part .no { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 44pt; line-height: 0.8; color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 1.4pt var(--navy); }
.part .no.fill { color: var(--acc); -webkit-text-stroke: 0; }
.part .ttl .e { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 18pt; color: var(--navy); line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.01em; }
.part .ttl .k { font-size: 9.6pt; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); margin-top: 1.2mm; }
.part .meta { text-align: right; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); line-height: 1.35; }
.part .meta .time { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; color: var(--acc); font-size: 13pt; display: block; }
.qr { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 13mm; height: 13mm; border: 0.8pt dashed #9aa0ab; font-size: 5.8pt; color: var(--gray); text-align: center; line-height: 1.2; margin-left: 3mm; vertical-align: bottom; }
.part .meta-wrap { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; }
h3.pt { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 2.5mm; margin: 4.5mm 0 2mm; font-size: 11pt; font-weight: 800; color: var(--ink); }
h3.pt .n { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: #fff; background: var(--navy); font-size: 7.6pt; padding: 0.6mm 1.8mm; letter-spacing: 0.08em; }
h3.pt .n.o { background: var(--acc); }
h3.pt small { font-weight: 500; color: var(--gray); font-size: 8pt; margin-left: auto; }
.lead { margin: 0 0 3mm; color: #33363d; }
/* 판서노트 표 */
table.note { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.9pt; }
table.note th { text-align: left; font-size: 8pt; color: var(--gray); font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding: 1.2mm 1.5mm; }
table.note td { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.9mm 1.5mm; vertical-align: top; }
table.note td.k { font-weight: 700; width: 46mm; }
table.note td.v { width: 30mm; }
.blank { display: inline-block; min-width: 18mm; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--acc); text-align: center; color: transparent; }
.ex div { margin: 0.4mm 0; }
.ok { color: var(--acc); font-weight: 800; }
.chk { display: inline-block; width: 3.1mm; height: 3.1mm; border: 0.7pt solid #7d828c; vertical-align: -0.4mm; margin: 0 0.6mm; }
ol.q { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; counter-reset: q; }
ol.q > li { counter-increment: q; position: relative; padding-left: 7.5mm; margin-bottom: 2.1mm; }
ol.q > li::before { content: counter(q); position: absolute; left: 0; top: -0.3mm; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); font-size: 9pt; }
.cols2 { column-count: 2; column-gap: 7mm; column-rule: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); }
.cols2 > * { break-inside: avoid; }
.c { font-weight: 700; white-space: nowrap; }
.ox { float: right; color: var(--gray); font-family: Inter; font-weight: 600; font-size: 8pt; }
.wl { display: inline-block; border-bottom: 0.6pt solid #8b9099; min-width: 30mm; height: 4mm; vertical-align: bottom; }
.line { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid #b9bdc5; height: 7mm; }
.passage { margin: 1mm 0 2.5mm; text-align: justify; }
.src { font-family: Inter; font-size: 7pt; color: var(--acc); font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.qhead { font-weight: 800; margin: 0 0 1.4mm; font-size: 9.2pt; }
.qhead .src { margin-left: 1.5mm; }
.opts { font-size: 8.6pt; margin: 0 0 1mm; }
.opts div { margin: 0.4mm 0; }
.gloss { font-size: 7.2pt; color: var(--gray); text-align: right; margin-top: -1mm; margin-bottom: 1.5mm; }
.rd { break-inside: avoid; margin-bottom: 5mm; }
.pat { margin-bottom: 4.6mm; }
.pat .f { display: inline-block; font-family: Inter; font-weight: 800; font-size: 9pt; color: #fff; background: var(--ink); padding: 0.6mm 2.2mm; margin-right: 2mm; }
.pat .fk { font-weight: 700; }
.pat .s { margin: 1.6mm 0 0 0; }
.cond { font-size: 8.4pt; color: #333; border-top: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.4mm 0; margin: 1.2mm 0 2mm; }
.cond b { color: var(--navy); margin-right: 2mm; }
.bogi { font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.8pt; text-align: center; padding: 1.6mm 0; border-top: 1pt solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); margin: 1.2mm 0 2mm; word-spacing: 1.5mm; }
.tr { margin-bottom: 2.4mm; }
.tr .no { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--navy); margin-right: 1.5mm; font-size: 8.6pt; }
/* voca */
table.voc { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.7pt; }
table.voc td { padding: 1.35mm 1mm; border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); }
table.voc td.n { width: 6mm; font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: #a3a8b2; font-size: 7pt; }
table.voc td.w { font-family: Inter; font-weight: 700; width: 33mm; }
table.voc td.b { width: 30mm; }
/* plan */
table.grid { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.7pt; }
table.grid th { text-align: left; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding: 1.4mm 1.5mm; }
table.grid td { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 2mm 1.5mm; }
table.grid td.no { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); width: 10mm; }
.score { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.2fr 1fr 1fr 1.4fr; border-top: 2pt solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 0.6pt solid var(--ink); margin-bottom: 4mm; }
.score div { padding: 1.6mm 2.5mm; border-right: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); height: 13mm; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); }
.score div:last-child { border-right: 0; }
.score b { display: block; color: var(--ink); font-size: 8.2pt; }
.key h4 { font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 8.6pt; color: var(--navy); margin: 3.4mm 0 1.2mm; letter-spacing: 0.04em; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding-bottom: 0.8mm; }
.key h4 span { font-family: Pretendard; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); margin-left: 1.5mm; }
.key .row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.6mm 4.5mm; font-size: 8.4pt; }
.key .row b { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); margin-right: 1mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 8.2pt; margin: 0.6mm 0; }
.key .ls b { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); margin-right: 1.5mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
/* cover */
.cover { padding: 0; color: #fff; background: radial-gradient(120% 80% at 75% 35%, #2d3f86 0%, #17214a 45%, #0b1024 100%); }
.cover svg.art { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 210mm; height: 297mm; }
.cover .top { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 16mm; top: 15mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 8.6pt; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.cover .pill { border: 0.8pt solid rgba(255,255,255,.75); border-radius: 10mm; padding: 1mm 3.2mm; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .series { opacity: .85; font-weight: 500; }
.cover .title { position: absolute; left: 16mm; top: 30mm; }
.cover .title .over { font-size: 11pt; font-weight: 600; opacity: .9; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
.cover .title h1 { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; font-weight: 400; font-size: 84pt; line-height: 1.02; margin: 2mm 0 0; letter-spacing: -0.01em; }
.cover .title h1 span { color: var(--acc2); }
.cover .title .sub { margin-top: 4mm; font-size: 13pt; font-weight: 700; display: flex; gap: 3mm; align-items: center; }
.cover .title .sub i { font-style: normal; font-weight: 500; opacity: .8; font-size: 10pt; }
.cover .band { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 64mm; background: #f2ff6b; color: var(--ink); padding: 9mm 16mm 0; }
.cover .band .who { font-size: 9.5pt; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .band .who b { color: #2440b3; }
.cover .band .slogan { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; font-size: 33pt; line-height: 1.1; margin-top: 2mm; }
.cover .band .feat { position: absolute; right: 16mm; top: 9mm; text-align: right; font-size: 8.2pt; line-height: 1.75; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .band .feat span { display: inline-block; background: var(--ink); color: #f2ff6b; padding: 0 2mm; margin-left: 1mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.cover .band .bot { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 16mm; bottom: 9mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 8.4pt; font-weight: 700; }
.cover .band .bot span { font-weight: 500; }
.memo { margin-top: 5mm; }
.memo .mh { font-family: "Archivo Black", Pretendard; font-size: 7.6pt; color: var(--navy); letter-spacing: .06em; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding-bottom: .8mm; }
.memo .line { border-bottom: .5pt dashed #c3c7cf; }
table.tf { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.4pt; margin-bottom: 1mm; }
table.tf td { border-bottom: .5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.2mm .5mm; }
table.tf td.b { width: 12mm; text-align: right; color: var(--gray); }
.sum { font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.6pt; border-top: .5pt solid var(--rule); border-bottom: .5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.3mm 0; margin: 0 0 1.4mm; }
.pair { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.4pt; row-gap: .5mm; }
.q2 { margin-top: 3mm; }

:root { --brand: #213f93; --navy: #213f93; --tint: #eaf1fb; --tint2: #cfdcf2; --acc: #ff6a2b; --ink: #1a1d26; }
.page { padding: 19mm 16mm 15mm 14mm; }
.en { font-family: "Source Serif 4", Georgia, serif; font-size: 9.7pt; line-height: 1.6; letter-spacing: 0; }
/* header band */
.run { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; height: 11mm; margin: 0; padding: 0 16mm 0 14mm; background: var(--tint); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 7.6pt; color: var(--brand); }
.run .brand { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; padding: 1.2mm 2.6mm; font-size: 7.4pt; letter-spacing: .08em; }
.run .brand i { color: #ffd36b; }
.cover .run { display: none; }
/* thumb index */
.thumb { position: absolute; right: 0; width: 7.5mm; height: 27mm; background: var(--tint2); color: var(--brand); border-radius: 2mm 0 0 2mm; writing-mode: vertical-rl; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 6.6pt; letter-spacing: .12em; }
.thumb.on { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; }
/* part head */
.part { border-bottom: 1.2pt solid var(--brand); padding-bottom: 2.6mm; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: center; }
.part .no, .part .no.fill { font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 21pt; line-height: 1; color: #fff; -webkit-text-stroke: 0; background: var(--brand); padding: 2.2mm 3mm 2mm; border-radius: 1.6mm; }
.part .ttl .e { color: var(--brand); font-size: 16pt; }
.part .meta .time { color: var(--acc); }
/* section chips */
h3.pt .n { background: var(--brand); border-radius: 1mm; }
h3.pt .n.o { background: var(--acc); }
/* point boxes */
.box { border: .8pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 2.6mm; margin: 0 0 4mm; overflow: hidden; }
.box > h3.pt { margin: 0 0 2mm; background: var(--tint); padding: 1.8mm 3mm; }
.box > :not(h3) { margin-left: 3.5mm !important; margin-right: 3.5mm !important; }
.box > :last-child { margin-bottom: 3mm !important; }
/* 판서 빈칸 */
.blank { color: transparent; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--acc); position: relative; min-width: 15mm; }
table.note td.v { width: 40mm; white-space: nowrap; }
table.note td.k { width: 50mm; }
.blank i { position: absolute; left: 0; top: -0.5mm; color: var(--acc); font-style: normal; font-weight: 800; font-size: 8pt; }
/* choice box */
.c { white-space: nowrap; font-weight: 600; }
.c b { display: inline-block; border: .7pt solid #8796b8; padding: 0 1.4mm; line-height: 1.35; font-weight: 600; }
.c b + b { border-left: 0; }
/* tables */
table.note th, table.grid th { color: var(--brand); border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--brand); background: var(--tint); }
table.grid td.no { color: var(--brand); }
ol.q > li::before { color: var(--brand); font-family: "Archivo Black"; content: counter(q, decimal-leading-zero); }
ol.q > li { padding-left: 8mm; }
.exwrap { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 38mm; column-gap: 5mm; }
.vside { border-left: .6pt solid var(--tint2); padding-left: 3mm; font-size: 7.8pt; line-height: 1.55; }
.vside h5 { margin: 0 0 1.5mm; font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 7pt; color: var(--brand); letter-spacing: .08em; }
.vside div { margin-bottom: 1.2mm; }
.vside div span { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-weight: 600; display: block; color: var(--ink); font-size: 8.3pt; }
.score { border-top: 1.4pt solid var(--brand); }
.key h4 { color: var(--brand); border-bottom-color: var(--brand); }
.memo .mh { color: var(--brand); border-bottom-color: var(--brand); }
.foot .pg { color: var(--brand); }
.tip b { background: var(--acc); }
.src { color: var(--acc); }
.cover .band .who b { color: var(--brand); }

.qc { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; column-gap: 7mm; row-gap: 1.6mm; }
.qc > div { position: relative; padding-left: 7mm; }
.qc > div > em { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; font-style: normal; font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--brand); font-size: 8.4pt; }
.fillw { display: inline-block; min-width: 16mm; border-bottom: .6pt solid #8b9099; }
.abc { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-size: 8.8pt; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 6mm 1fr 1fr 1fr; row-gap: .4mm; margin-top: 1.5mm; }
.abc span.h { color: var(--gray); font-family: Pretendard; font-size: 7.8pt; }

.key .row { font-size: 7.9pt; gap: 0.3mm 3.6mm; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 7.7pt; margin: 0.3mm 0; }
.key h4 { margin: 2.2mm 0 0.8mm; }
.bogi2 { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-size: 8.8pt; text-align: center; border: .7pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 1.5mm; background: var(--tint); padding: 1.3mm 0; margin: 0 0 2mm; word-spacing: 2mm; }

table.note td { padding: 1.3mm 1.2mm; font-size: 8.3pt; }
table.note td.k { width: 40mm !important; }
table.note td.v { width: 33mm !important; white-space: normal !important; }
table.note td.en { font-size: 8.9pt; line-height: 1.45; }
.key .row { font-size: 7.6pt !important; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 7.5pt !important; }
/* 예비고3 WEEK 02: 긴 문장용 간격 */
.qc.en { font-size: 8.5pt; line-height: 1.4; row-gap: 1.1mm !important; }
ol.q.en { font-size: 8.6pt; line-height: 1.4; }
ol.q.en > li { margin-bottom: 1.1mm; }
.bgrid .bb .ex div { font-size: 8.3pt !important; line-height: 1.42 !important; }
.bgrid .bx { line-height: 1.5 !important; margin-bottom: .6mm !important; }
.bgrid .bb { margin-bottom: 2.4mm !important; }
.box { margin-bottom: 3mm; }
.box > h3.pt { margin-bottom: 1.4mm; }
.box .ex div { font-size: 8.6pt; line-height: 1.45; }
.pat { margin-bottom: 3.2mm; }
.pat .line { height: 6mm; }

table.note th { text-align: left; font-size: 8pt; color: var(--gray); font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding: 1.2mm 1.5mm; }
table.note td { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.9mm 1.5mm; vertical-align: top; }
table.note td.k { font-weight: 700; width: 46mm; }
table.note td.v { width: 30mm; }
.blank { display: inline-block; min-width: 18mm; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--acc); text-align: center; color: transparent; }
.ex div { margin: 0.4mm 0; }
.ok { color: var(--acc); font-weight: 800; }
.chk { display: inline-block; width: 3.1mm; height: 3.1mm; border: 0.7pt solid #7d828c; vertical-align: -0.4mm; margin: 0 0.6mm; }
ol.q { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; counter-reset: q; }
ol.q > li { counter-increment: q; position: relative; padding-left: 7.5mm; margin-bottom: 2.1mm; }
ol.q > li::before { content: counter(q); position: absolute; left: 0; top: -0.3mm; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); font-size: 9pt; }
.cols2 { column-count: 2; column-gap: 7mm; column-rule: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); }
.cols2 > * { break-inside: avoid; }
.c { font-weight: 700; white-space: nowrap; }
.ox { float: right; color: var(--gray); font-family: Inter; font-weight: 600; font-size: 8pt; }
ol.q > li { display: flow-root; }
.wl { display: inline-block; border-bottom: 0.6pt solid #8b9099; min-width: 30mm; height: 4mm; vertical-align: bottom; }
.line { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid #b9bdc5; height: 7mm; }
.passage { margin: 1mm 0 2.5mm; text-align: justify; }
.src { font-family: Inter; font-size: 7pt; color: var(--acc); font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.qhead { font-weight: 800; margin: 0 0 1.4mm; font-size: 9.2pt; }
.qhead .src { margin-left: 1.5mm; }
.opts { font-size: 8.6pt; margin: 0 0 1mm; }
.opts div { margin: 0.4mm 0; }
.gloss { font-size: 7.2pt; color: var(--gray); text-align: right; margin-top: -1mm; margin-bottom: 1.5mm; }
.rd { break-inside: avoid; margin-bottom: 5mm; }
.pat { margin-bottom: 4.6mm; }
.pat .f { display: inline-block; font-family: Inter; font-weight: 800; font-size: 9pt; color: #fff; background: var(--ink); padding: 0.6mm 2.2mm; margin-right: 2mm; }
.pat .fk { font-weight: 700; }
.pat .s { margin: 1.6mm 0 0 0; }
.cond { font-size: 8.4pt; color: #333; border-top: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.4mm 0; margin: 1.2mm 0 2mm; }
.cond b { color: var(--navy); margin-right: 2mm; }
.bogi { font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.8pt; text-align: center; padding: 1.6mm 0; border-top: 1pt solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); margin: 1.2mm 0 2mm; word-spacing: 1.5mm; }
.tr { margin-bottom: 2.4mm; }
.tr .no { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--navy); margin-right: 1.5mm; font-size: 8.6pt; }
/* voca */
table.voc { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.7pt; }
table.voc td { padding: 1.35mm 1mm; border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); }
table.voc td.n { width: 6mm; font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: #a3a8b2; font-size: 7pt; }
table.voc td.w { font-family: Inter; font-weight: 700; width: 33mm; }
table.voc td.b { width: 30mm; }
/* plan */
table.grid { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.7pt; }
table.grid th { text-align: left; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding: 1.4mm 1.5mm; }
table.grid td { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 2mm 1.5mm; }
table.grid td.no { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); width: 10mm; }
.score { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.2fr 1fr 1fr 1.4fr; border-top: 2pt solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 0.6pt solid var(--ink); margin-bottom: 4mm; }
.score div { padding: 1.6mm 2.5mm; border-right: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); height: 13mm; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); }
.score div:last-child { border-right: 0; }
.score b { display: block; color: var(--ink); font-size: 8.2pt; }
.key h4 { font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 8.6pt; color: var(--navy); margin: 3.4mm 0 1.2mm; letter-spacing: 0.04em; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding-bottom: 0.8mm; }
.key h4 span { font-family: Pretendard; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); margin-left: 1.5mm; }
.key .row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.6mm 4.5mm; font-size: 8.4pt; }
.key .row b { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); margin-right: 1mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 8.2pt; margin: 0.6mm 0; }
.key .ls b { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); margin-right: 1.5mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
/* cover */
.cover { padding: 0; color: #fff; background: radial-gradient(120% 80% at 75% 35%, #2d3f86 0%, #17214a 45%, #0b1024 100%); }
.cover svg.art { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 210mm; height: 297mm; }
.cover .top { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 16mm; top: 15mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 8.6pt; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.cover .pill { border: 0.8pt solid rgba(255,255,255,.75); border-radius: 10mm; padding: 1mm 3.2mm; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .series { opacity: .85; font-weight: 500; }
.cover .title { position: absolute; left: 16mm; top: 30mm; }
.cover .title .over { font-size: 11pt; font-weight: 600; opacity: .9; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
.cover .title h1 { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; font-weight: 400; font-size: 84pt; line-height: 1.02; margin: 2mm 0 0; letter-spacing: -0.01em; }
.cover .title h1 span { color: var(--acc2); }
.cover .title .sub { margin-top: 4mm; font-size: 13pt; font-weight: 700; display: flex; gap: 3mm; align-items: center; }
.cover .title .sub i { font-style: normal; font-weight: 500; opacity: .8; font-size: 10pt; }
.cover .band { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 64mm; background: #f2ff6b; color: var(--ink); padding: 9mm 16mm 0; }
.cover .band .who { font-size: 9.5pt; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .band .who b { color: #2440b3; }
.cover .band .slogan { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; font-size: 33pt; line-height: 1.1; margin-top: 2mm; }
.cover .band .feat { position: absolute; right: 16mm; top: 9mm; text-align: right; font-size: 8.2pt; line-height: 1.75; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .band .feat span { display: inline-block; background: var(--ink); color: #f2ff6b; padding: 0 2mm; margin-left: 1mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.cover .band .bot { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 16mm; bottom: 9mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 8.4pt; font-weight: 700; }
.cover .band .bot span { font-weight: 500; }
.memo { margin-top: 5mm; }
.memo .mh { font-family: "Archivo Black", Pretendard; font-size: 7.6pt; color: var(--navy); letter-spacing: .06em; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding-bottom: .8mm; }
.memo .line { border-bottom: .5pt dashed #c3c7cf; }
table.tf { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.4pt; margin-bottom: 1mm; }
table.tf td { border-bottom: .5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.2mm .5mm; }
table.tf td.b { width: 12mm; text-align: right; color: var(--gray); }
.sum { font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.6pt; border-top: .5pt solid var(--rule); border-bottom: .5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.3mm 0; margin: 0 0 1.4mm; }
.pair { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.4pt; row-gap: .5mm; }
.q2 { margin-top: 3mm; }

.page { padding: 19mm 16mm 15mm 14mm; }
.en { font-family: "Source Serif 4", Georgia, serif; font-size: 9.7pt; line-height: 1.6; letter-spacing: 0; }

.run { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; height: 11mm; margin: 0; padding: 0 16mm 0 14mm; background: var(--tint); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 7.6pt; color: var(--brand); }
.run .brand { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; padding: 1.2mm 2.6mm; font-size: 7.4pt; letter-spacing: .08em; }
.run .brand i { color: #ffd36b; }
.cover .run { display: none; }
/* thumb index */
.thumb { position: absolute; right: 0; width: 7.5mm; height: 27mm; background: var(--tint2); color: var(--brand); border-radius: 2mm 0 0 2mm; writing-mode: vertical-rl; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 6.6pt; letter-spacing: .12em; }
.thumb.on { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; }

.part { border-bottom: 1.2pt solid var(--brand); padding-bottom: 2.6mm; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: center; }
.part .no, .part .no.fill { font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 21pt; line-height: 1; color: #fff; -webkit-text-stroke: 0; background: var(--brand); padding: 2.2mm 3mm 2mm; border-radius: 1.6mm; }
.part .ttl .e { color: var(--brand); font-size: 16pt; }
.part .meta .time { color: var(--acc); }
/* section chips */
h3.pt .n { background: var(--brand); border-radius: 1mm; }
h3.pt .n.o { background: var(--acc); }
/* point boxes */
.box { border: .8pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 2.6mm; margin: 0 0 4mm; overflow: hidden; }
.box > h3.pt { margin: 0 0 2mm; background: var(--tint); padding: 1.8mm 3mm; }
.box > :not(h3) { margin-left: 3.5mm !important; margin-right: 3.5mm !important; }
.box > :last-child { margin-bottom: 3mm !important; }

table.note td.v { width: 40mm; white-space: nowrap; }

.c { white-space: nowrap; font-weight: 600; }
.c b { display: inline-block; border: .7pt solid #8796b8; padding: 0 1.4mm; line-height: 1.35; font-weight: 600; }
.c b + b { border-left: 0; }

table.grid td.no { color: var(--brand); }

ol.q > li { padding-left: 8mm; }
.exwrap { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 38mm; column-gap: 5mm; }
.vside { border-left: .6pt solid var(--tint2); padding-left: 3mm; font-size: 7.8pt; line-height: 1.55; }
.vside h5 { margin: 0 0 1.5mm; font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 7pt; color: var(--brand); letter-spacing: .08em; }
.vside div { margin-bottom: 1.2mm; }

.cover .band .who b { color: var(--brand); }

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

동사의 수는 동사 바로 앞 명사가 아니라 진짜 주어가 정한다.

01명사 주어 — 수식어는 괄호로 지운다

수식어(전치사구·분사구·관계사절)는 괄호로 묶어 지우고, 남은 머리 명사에 수를 맞춘다.

수식어 속 수식어(이중 수식), 콤마·대시로 끼운 삽입구가 겹쳐도 → 모두 ( )로 → 맨 앞 머리 명사 하나만 남긴다.

[The decline] (in the number of bees) (that pollinate crops in many regions), (according to recent reports,) threatens global food security.[ ] 진짜 주어 · ( ) 지울 수식어 · 밑줄 동사
The rapid spread of rumors on social networks, which reach millions before any correction appears, poses a threat to democratic debate.
The fossils discovered beneath the ancient lake, unlike those found elsewhere, suggest that the climate changed abruptly.
동사 바로 앞의 appears · elsewhere에 속지 말 것 — 콤마 삽입은 통째로 지운다.

02동명사구 · to부정사구 · 명사절 주어 = 단수

-ing · To · That · What · Whether · How로 시작하는 주어 덩어리는 「~하는 것」 하나 → 단수 동사.

주어 모양해석동사
Getting ~ / To learn ~~하는 것은단수
That / What / Whether / How + S + V~라는 것 / ~하는 것 / ~인지 / ~하는 방식단수
Recognizing the limits of one’s own knowledge, especially in fields where experts disagree, is the first step toward intellectual growth.
What the archaeologists found beneath the abandoned houses was a collection of tools hidden from invaders.
단, 「-ing ~ and -ing ~」처럼 서로 다른 두 덩어리가 and로 이어지면 복수.

03주격 관계대명사 + 동사 — 선행사에 맞춘다

관계사절 안의 동사는 who · which · that 바로 앞 명사, 곧 선행사의 수에 맞춘다.

who (I believe) is — 관계사 바로 뒤 삽입절(I think · they say)은 지우고 선행사에 맞춘다. 문장 전체 동사는 따로 맨 앞 주어에.

Scholars who insist that ancient myths contain no historical truth often overlook the archaeological evidence that supports at least some of the stories passed down through generations of oral tradition.
The engineer who, her colleagues believe, deserves credit for the design has refused the award.
one of the + 복수명사 + who → 복수 / the only one of the + 복수명사 + who → 단수.

All the philosophical dilemmas about whether translation “reflects” or instead “transforms” what’s in the original need to be swept aside. This is exactly the dichotomy that Merleau-Ponty’s account of perception is trying to free us from: are we “seeing” objects or “constituting” them? Neither, because we perceive things in a world we live in and have the power to transform: a chair is something we can go sit in; a mug is something we can pick up. One of Merleau-Ponty’s many great metaphors is that perception neither finds the world nor creates it: it reveals it, which he expresses using the term révélateur, the developing fluid for photographs in a darkroom. The act of seeing develops what’s in the world, like developing a photograph. Likewise, a translation “develops the photograph” of the original text. Translators don’t simply “recognize” what’s there, but nor are we “changing” it into anything it isn’t already, though we can be more or less aggressively interventionist in our darkroom. As a translator I take up the affordances of the original, moving through its world and constantly invited to respond in certain ways.

⑤ fixes the original text so that it can never be changed again

We use space, eye contact, and touch to communicate positive and negative attitudes toward others. These signals can reflect and regulate the intimacy in a relationship. In one interesting application of this idea, researchers found that nonverbal intimacy regulation even occurs when people interact with others via avatars in online environments. As in face-to-face encounters, people typically respond to decreased distances by compensating with reduced gaze. But we should keep in mind what communication scholar Mark Knapp has pointed out: These stereotypical immediacy behaviors—close distances, eye contact, touch, body lean, and so forth—are more evident during the early stages of intimacy than they are during later stages. When people become comfortable with each other, they may become more selective in their use of nonverbal immediacy signals, using them during a personal crisis, after a fight, on special occasions, at particular social gatherings, and the like. They may also adopt other more idiosyncratic ways of showing their affection—a unique gesture or a special touch, for instance—and they may feel less obliged overall to display their affections in public.

In many situations, corporate moral decisions do not entail a trade-off: doing the right thing is sometimes good for business. BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

주어가 동작을 하면 능동태, 동작을 받으면 수동태. 수능은 긴 수식어 · 삽입 뒤에서 이 판단을 묻는다.

01능동 vs 수동 — 주어가 하는가, 당하는가

주어가 동작을 하면 능동, 받으면 수동 be + p.p.. 타동사 뒤 목적어 자리가 비어 있으면 수동을 의심하고, 주어와 동사 사이의 수식어는 괄호로 지운다.

능동The engineers who designed the bridge across the bay inspect its steel cables every winter, when sudden storms put the greatest strain on the structure.
수동The steel cables of the bridge across the bay, which carry thousands of vehicles a day, are inspected every winter by engineers trained in structural safety.

주의주어 뒤 관계사절의 동사(carry)와 문장의 본동사(are inspected)를 헷갈리지 말 것.

023형식 → 수동태 (by 생략)

목적어 → 주어 자리, 동사 → be + p.p.(시제는 be동사가), 원래 주어 → by + 목적격. 행위자가 막연하거나 뻔하면 by 이하는 생략한다.

Critics praised the novel → The novel was praised → (by critics)
능동Critics across Europe praised the novel for its honest portrait of rural poverty long before it was translated into English for American readers.
생략Thousands of tons of food are thrown away every day in wealthy countries, even though millions of people elsewhere still struggle to find enough to eat.

학평·수능29번은 타동사 뒤 목적어 자리가 비었는지(수동) · 찼는지(능동)로 묻는다.

034형식 수동태 — 목적어가 둘이면 주어도 둘

간접목적어가 주어면 직접목적어가 p.p. 뒤에 남는다. 직접목적어가 주어면 「전치사 + 간접목적어」 — give류 to, make · buy류 for, ask는 of.

전치사동사꼴
togive · send · show · teach · tell · lend · offer · awardwas sent to + 사람
formake · buy · cook · get · build · findwas bought for + 사람
ofaskwas asked of + 사람
간접Every researcher who joined the project in its first year was given full access to the collection of letters that the founder had kept secret for decades.
직접Full access to the collection of letters that the founder had kept secret for decades was given to every researcher who joined the project in its first year.

주의make · buy · cook은 보통 직접목적어를 주어로: A gift was bought for her (○)

045형식 수동태 — 목적격보어는 남는다

목적어만 주어 자리로 가고 목적격보어(명사 · 형용사 · to부정사 · 분사)는 p.p. 뒤에 그대로 남는다. consider · call · elect · keep · find가 단골.

명사The young economist, whose controversial theory had been dismissed by most of her colleagues, was later considered one of the most original thinkers of her generation.
to-vPassengers traveling on international flights are required to declare any food products they carry, since even a single piece of fruit can bring plant diseases into the country.

05지각 · 사역동사 수동태 — 원형이 to부정사로

make · see · hear의 원형 보어는 수동태에서 to부정사로. -ing 보어는 그대로, let은 be allowed to로.

made them work → were made to work → saw her leaving → was seen leaving
사역The miners trapped underground after the collapse were made to wait nearly two days before rescue teams could safely reach the tunnel where they had taken shelter.
-ingThe missing hiker was last seen walking toward the northern ridge, where sudden fog had already forced several climbers to turn back.

학평·수능be made + 원형(×) → be made to + 원형(○)이 단골.

06시제 · 준동사의 수동형 — 시제는 be동사가

진행 be + being + p.p., 완료 have + been + p.p., 조동사 + be + p.p. 준동사도 의미상 주어가 「당하면」 수동형.

형태꼴예 (explain · ignore)
진행be + being + p.p.are being explained
완료have · has · had + been + p.p.have been explained
조동사will · can · must + be + p.p.will be explained
준동사to be p.p. · being p.p. · having been p.p.hate being ignored
진행A new set of safety rules for deep-sea drilling is being drafted by an international panel that was formed after the oil spill devastated the coastline last year.
준동사Many celebrities who complain about the press secretly dislike being ignored even more than being criticized, since attention, whether positive or negative, keeps their names alive.

주의being · been을 빠뜨리면 틀린다.

07구동사 수동태 — 전치사 · 부사도 함께

look after · put off · laugh at · deal with · rely on은 한 덩어리 동사라 수동태에서도 전치사 · 부사를 빠뜨리지 않는다.

수동The complaints raised by residents near the airport have never been properly dealt with by the authorities, who insist the noise is within legal limits.
수동The opening ceremony of the international film festival was put off until the following week because the main theater had been badly damaged by a flood.

주의was laughed (×) → was laughed at (○)

08수동태로 쓸 수 없는 동사

종류동사
자동사happen · occur · take place · appear · disappear · arise · emerge · exist · remain · consist of · result in · belong to
상태동사resemble · have(가지다) · lack · fit · cost
자동Serious disagreements arose among the members of the research team when the data from the final experiment contradicted the hypothesis they had defended for years.
자동The committee that will choose the winner of this year’s prize consists of three novelists, two literary critics, and a librarian chosen by public vote.

학평·수능was occurred · is consisted of · were disappeared · is resembled가 29번 오답 단골.

09감정동사 — 주면 -ing, 느끼면 p.p.

감정을 일으키는 쪽이면 -ing, 느끼는 쪽이면 p.p.. 사람이라도 남에게 감정을 주면 -ing.

-ingThe results of the ten-year study on childhood nutrition were so disappointing that the foundation stopped funding the research altogether.
p.p.Affluent investors who had expected record profits were shocked to learn that the company had incurred losses for the third quarter in a row.

주의a boring lecturer(남을 지루하게 하는 강사) / a bored audience(지루해진 청중)

10절의 수동태 — It is said that ~ / be said to

① It + be p.p. + that절 ② that절 주어 + be p.p. + to부정사. that절이 주절보다 앞선 일이면 to have p.p.

People believe that the temple was built in 1200 → It is believed that the temple was built in 1200 → The temple is believed to have been built in 1200
ItIt is widely believed that regular contact with nature lowers stress and improves concentration, although the evidence for these effects remains surprisingly limited.
완료The ancient bridge is thought to have been built by local farmers rather than trained engineers, since its design differs greatly from Roman structures of the same period.

학평·수능be said(believed · thought) to 뒤 「원형 vs have p.p.」 — 시간 차이를 묻는다.

A telescoping of time correlates with size. Small animals’ reflexes must be quicker in order to control much smaller limbs and respond to rapid locomotor feedback. Further, decision making must be streamlined in small species because their high metabolic rates and minimal energy reserves offer few choices in food-searching activities, defending against predators, or mating behaviors. And, perhaps most important, a short lifetime offers little time for learning from experience. As a result, being short-lived puts a premium on the effectiveness of preprogrammed behavior patterns that require little in the way of environmental fine-tuning. Large animals, in comparison, can get by with rather slower reflexes, can afford to vary their mating and food-searching behaviors in an effort to better optimize their behaviors, and may have a considerable opportunity to learn by observation and trial and error. Being longer-lived puts a greater premium on learning and memory, and less on automatic preprogrammed behaviors. In addition, living a long time or having the capacity to travel for long distances is more likely to expose an animal to significant changes in the environment.

CHAPTER 04 동사와 준동사 구분
강의 40분

한 절에서 본동사는 하나, 나머지 동사 모양은 준동사(to-v · -ing · p.p.)다. 수능은 긴 주어 · 삽입 · 생략 뒤에서 이 구별을 묻는다.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

01한 절에 본동사는 하나

핵심접속사 없이 본동사는 하나. 나머지 동사 모양(to-v · -ing · p.p.)은 준동사다.

동사The engineers who designed the new dam inspected its foundations twice a year and reported even the smallest cracks to the authorities responsible for the region’s water supply.
준동사The government postponed the final vote on the controversial legislation for a week to give citizens more time to study its details.

주의and · but · or로 이은 동사는 앞 동사와 모양을 맞춘다(병렬): inspected … and reported

02동사 수 = 접속사 · 관계사 수 + 1

핵심접속사 · 관계사가 하나면 동사는 둘. 목적격 관계사가 생략되어도(명사 + S + V) 그 절의 동사를 센다.

The letters (that) the historian discovered → revealed … → 생략 관계사 1개 + 1 = 동사 2개
생략The letters and petitions the historian discovered in the basement of the old courthouse revealed a side of the former mayor that nobody in the town had suspected.
접속사Many sociologists argue that the rapid spread of smartphones has changed the way teenagers form friendships.

학평·수능관계사 생략 · 삽입절(I think · they say)이 낀 문장에서 동사 자리를 묻는 것이 29번 단골.

03주어 자리 — 동명사 · to부정사 · 명사절

핵심동사원형은 주어가 될 수 없다. -ing · to-v · 명사절(what · whether · that)로 쓰고 동사는 단수.

주어 모양예판정
동명사Ignoring early warning signs is risky.○
명사절What the survey revealed was alarming.○
동사원형Ignore early warning signs is risky.×
동명사Exposing young children to several languages at an early age seems to improve their ability to switch between tasks, although researchers have not yet reached a consensus on why.
명사절Whether the new congestion charge will actually reduce traffic in the city center remains unclear to most transportation experts.

주의문장 맨 앞의 동사원형은 명령문이 된다: Ignore the warning … (경고를 무시하라)

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ②

04목적어 자리 — -ing만 · to-v만

핵심enjoy · avoid · deny · postpone 뒤는 -ing, want · decide · afford · manage 뒤는 to-v.

뒤에 오는 것동사
-ing만enjoy · finish · avoid · mind · deny · postpone · consider · give up
to-v만want · decide · hope · plan · expect · afford · manage · refuse
-ingThe witness firmly denied having any contact with the suspect during the week before the burglary took place.
to-vAfter months of talks, the two companies finally agreed to share the cost of building a new research center.

학평·수능자세한 동명사 · to부정사 목적어는 5장에서 다시 다룬다.

05부사 자리 to-v — 「~하기 위해」

핵심문장이 다 끝난 뒤나 맨 앞에 오는 to-v는 목적(~하기 위해). 의미상 주어는 for + 목적격: in order for the plan to work

뒤Several hospitals have begun recording every conversation between doctors and patients to reduce misunderstandings about treatment.
앞To protect the marine life from further damage caused by pollutants, the government banned fishing boats from entering the bay for two years.

주의맨 앞 동사원형(Protect …, S + V)은 틀린다. 문두 -ing는 분사구문(~하면서)이라 뜻이 달라진다.

06명사 뒤 분사 — 꾸미는 말

핵심명사 바로 뒤 -ing(능동) · p.p.(수동)는 명사를 꾸미는 말이지 동사가 아니다. 타동사 뒤에 목적어가 있으면 -ing, 없으면(by ~) p.p.

[The paintings stolen …] → were returned → 진짜 동사는 were
p.p.The paintings stolen from the national gallery in 1990 were finally returned to the curator after an anonymous tip led the police to a farmhouse in the countryside.
-ingStudents applying for the scholarship must submit two letters of recommendation along with a short essay on their goals.

주의The paintings were stolen from the gallery were returned (×) — 동사가 둘이 된다.

07분사구문 — 문미 · 문두

핵심문미 「, -ing」는 동시 동작 · 결과. 문두 분사구문은 주절 주어가 하면 -ing, 당하면 p.p.

결과The river overflowed its banks after a week of heavy rain, forcing the authorities to evacuate thousands of residents from their homes in the middle of the night.
문두Written in plain language for ordinary readers, the report quickly became one of the most widely discussed documents of the year.

주의, forces (×) — 접속사 없이 동사를 더 쓸 수 없다. Writing in plain language, the report … (×) — 보고서는 쓰이는 대상.

08전치사 뒤 — 동명사

핵심in · by · without · before · instead of 뒤, 그리고 to가 전치사인 표현(object to · be used to · be committed to) 뒤에는 -ing.

withoutMany travelers book expensive tours without checking whether the same sites can be visited for free on their own.

09보어 자리 — 형용사 (부사 ×)

핵심be · remain · become · seem · feel 뒤, make · keep · find · consider + O 뒤는 형용사.

자리동사
주격 보어be · stay · remain · become · seem · look · sound · feel
목적격 보어make · keep · find · leave · consider + O + 형용사

10목적격 보어 — 원형 · to-v · -ing

핵심make · have · let + O + 원형, want · allow · enable · encourage + O + to-v, help는 둘 다.

동사목적격 보어
make · have · let동사원형
want · allow · enable · forceto부정사
help원형 / to부정사

enableCheap satellite imagery now enables farmers in remote regions to predict droughts weeks before their crops begin to fail and to plan their water use accordingly.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

to부정사는 「to + 동사원형」, 동명사는 「동사원형 + -ing」. 동사에서 나왔기 때문에 목적어 · 보어 · 수식어를 그대로 거느리고, 문장에서는 명사 · 형용사 · 부사로 일한다.

01to부정사 — 명사 역할 (주어 · 보어 · 목적어) · 가목적어 it

「~하는 것」. 주어가 길면 가주어 It ~ to-v, 목적어 자리면 make · find · think + it + 형용사 + to-v(가목적어). to부정사 주어는 단수 동사.

가주어It is extremely difficult to predict how a new species will behave once it has been introduced into an unfamiliar ecosystem.
가목적어The rapid spread of misinformation online has made it harder for scientists to communicate their research to the general public.

주의To verify every claim in the report are (×) → is (○) · made possible to-v (×) → made it possible to-v (○)

02to부정사 — 형용사 역할 (명사 뒤에서 꾸밈)

「~할 (명사)」. 명사 뒤에서 꾸미고, 동사가 자동사면 전치사까지 붙인다: a theory to rely on. the first · the last · the only 뒤에도 자주 온다.

수식Early farmers had few reliable ways to store grain through the winter, so a single poor harvest could threaten an entire village.
전치사Young researchers often lack a senior colleague to consult with when their experiments produce results that contradict existing theories.

주의a theory to rely (×) → a theory to rely on (○)

03to부정사 — 부사 역할 (목적 · 감정의 원인 · 판단 · 결과)

동사 · 형용사 · 문장 전체를 꾸민다. 가장 많이 나오는 것은 목적 「~하기 위해」, 고3 지문에는 only to-v 「(그러나) 결국 ~하고 말았다」도 잦다.

쓰임해석예
목적~하기 위해sold the car to pay the debt
감정의 원인~해서relieved to hear the news
판단의 근거~하다니foolish to trust him
결과(결국) ~하다hurried there, only to find it closed
목적To reduce the risk of flooding, engineers raised the riverbanks and built a series of channels that redirect excess water.
결과The explorers finally reached the summit after weeks of climbing, only to find that another team had planted its flag there the day before.

학평·수능문장 앞 「To-v ~, 주절」은 「~하기 위해」. 동사원형으로 시작하게 바꾼 오답이 단골.

바람 · 계획 · 결심 · 시도처럼 미래를 향한 동사는 to-v를 목적어로 쓴다.

즐기기 · 피하기 · 끝내기처럼 이미 하고 있거나 해 본 일의 동사는 -ing를 목적어로.

07둘 다 쓰지만 뜻이 다른 동사

to-v는 앞으로 할 일, -ing는 이미 한 일. stop · try · mean은 뜻 자체가 달라진다.

동사+ to-v+ -ing

학평·수능remember · forget · regret은 시간 단서로, mean은 「의도(to-v) / 의미(-ing)」로 판단.

Not only are our sensory systems organized to detect change, but they are most tuned to stimuli that are  . When you move your body and produce tactile sensations, these stimuli are less noticeable to you than are sensations produced by another individual. BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

분사는 동사에서 나온 형용사. 꾸밈을 받는 명사가 동작을 하면 -ing, 당하면 p.p. 고3 지문에서는 분사구가 길어져 주어와 본동사 사이가 멀어진다.

01현재분사 vs 과거분사 — 하는가, 당하는가

핵심명사가 스스로 하거나 진행 중이면 -ing(능동·진행), 당하거나 끝난 상태면 p.p.(수동·완료).

-ing (능동·진행)p.p. (수동·완료)
a declining population 줄어드는 인구a declined offer 거절된 제안
a developing country 개발도상국a developed country 선진국
-ingThe rising cost of housing in major cities has forced many young workers to move to suburban towns that are far from their offices.
p.p.The stolen paintings, which had been missing for nearly a century, were finally returned to the national gallery last spring.

주의falling leaves(떨어지는 잎) / fallen leaves(떨어진 잎) — 뜻이 달라진다.

02분사의 자리 · 분사 vs 본동사

핵심분사 한 단어는 명사 앞, 목적어 · 부사구가 붙은 분사구는 명사 뒤. 분사구가 주어에 붙어 길어져도 그 뒤에 본동사가 따로 있어야 한다.

앞Researchers have found that the sleeping brain continues to sort and store the information it took in during the day.
뒤The soil samples collected by the research team over the past decade show that the region is becoming drier every year.

학평·수능명사 + 분사구(= 주격 관계대명사 + be 생략) 뒤 동사 자리: The samples collected ~ showing (×) → show (○)

03감정 분사 — 감정을 주면 -ing, 느끼면 p.p.

핵심감정을 일으키는 쪽(사물·사람)은 -ing, 감정을 느끼는 쪽은 p.p.

동사-ingp.p.

-ingMany readers found the novel’s ending so disappointing that they wrote to the author asking for a sequel with a happier conclusion.
p.p.Investors alarmed by the sudden plunge in prices began selling their shares before the market closed that afternoon.

주의사람이라도 남을 지루하게 하면 -ing: a boring speaker / 지루함을 느끼면 bored listeners

As he reviewed → Reviewing the data, → the scientist noticed …

07분사구문의 능동 vs 수동

핵심문장의 주어가 그 동작을 하면 -ing, 당하면 p.p.로 시작한다(Being p.p.에서 Being 생략).

능동Recognizing the danger of the rising water, the villagers moved their livestock to higher ground hours before the dam finally broke.
수동Located at the crossroads of three major trade routes, the city grew wealthy long before any of its neighbors did.

주의분사구문의 주어 = 문장의 주어. 도시는 「위치한(놓인)」 대상이라 Located.

While a picture transports the spectator almost instantly into a landscape, language can only describe it detail by detail, bringing it slowly into the reader’s mind. How can a literary work capture the feel of a place in both its atmosphere and its topography without losing the reader in a descriptive forest? One solution, proposed by Balzac, is  . Balzac’s novels open with detailed portrayals of the setting, but the descriptions never threaten the reader’s sense of orientation because they trace a precise path through the fictional world. When the novel describes a house, the narrator inspects the building in a systematic manner, approaching it from the street, examining the garden and the front, entering through the main door, and walking from room to room, as would a real estate agent or a prospective resident. The reader ends up with a precise notion of the layout of the building, all the way down to the floor plan.

Surprise is the fundamental joke mechanism. Most punch lines rely on an element of surprise for their effect — that’s why they’re not funny the third time you hear them. The joke-teller’s skill lies in  . He must make a series of assumptions about what they will understand, what their reference points are, and how relaxed they appear to be. Jerry Seinfeld once compared telling a joke to attempting to leap a metaphorical canyon, taking the audience with you. The setup to the joke is the near-side cliff, and the punch line is the far side. If they’re too far apart, the listeners don’t make it to the other side. And if they are too close together, the audience just steps across the gap and doesn’t experience a thrilling leap of any kind. The joke-hearers get far more pleasure from the joke if they have to do a little work.

* canyon: 협곡

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

준동사(to부정사 · 동명사 · 분사)에도 행위자 · 시간 · 태가 있다. 의미상 주어 · 완료형 · 수동형을 모양으로 익힌다.

01to부정사의 의미상 주어 — for + 목적격

핵심to부정사의 행위자가 문장 주어와 다르면 to 앞에 for + 목적격을 쓴다. 가주어 It 구문 · too ~ to · enough to에서 자주 나온다.

It is nearly impossible + for small nations + to adapt
forIt is nearly impossible for small island nations to adapt to rising sea levels without unprecedented amounts of financial support from wealthier countries, many of which are themselves struggling with large budget deficits.
tooThe instructions in the manual were too technical for most first-time users to follow without calling the customer service center.

주의의미상 주어가 일반 사람(we · people)이면 for ~를 생략한다.

02사람의 성격 형용사 — of + 목적격

핵심kind · nice · wise · careless · foolish · rude · generous처럼 사람의 성격을 말하는 형용사 뒤에는 of + 목적격.

형용사의미상 주어
important · easy · hard · necessary · naturalfor + 목적격 (일에 대한 판단)
kind · nice · wise · careless · foolish · rude · generousof + 목적격 (사람에 대한 판단)
ofIt was considerate of the hospital staff to translate the consent forms into several languages for patients who could not read English.
ofIt was foolish of the investors to assume that a company with no record of profits and no clear strategy for complying with new regulations would keep growing indefinitely.

학평·수능「It is + 형용사 + [for / of] + 목적격 + to-v」 고르기가 단골.

03동명사의 의미상 주어 — 소유격(목적격)

핵심동명사의 행위자가 문장 주어와 다르면 동명사 앞에 소유격을 쓴다. 일상 영어에서는 목적격도 쓴다. 심화 there 구문이면 there being · for there to be.

소유격The committee strongly objected to the director’s appointing his own relatives to key positions in the foundation, which it regarded as a threat to the integrity of the organization.
목적격The success of the vaccine campaign depended on local leaders persuading reluctant families that the injections were safe.
thereMany economists worry about there being too few young workers to support a rapidly aging population.

주의주격(he · they) + -ing는 틀린다: they being late (×) → their being late (○)

Our choices and actions send messages to others about our values.

(A) This mixed signals problem is channeled into a simple question: what should be rewarded? In many cases, performance is multidimensional, but compensation is only given to one aspect of performance, typically the one that is easiest to measure. Simple “one-aspect” compensation sends a clear message to the workers: concentrate on what we’re paying you for and ignore everything else.

(B) Consider a manager who communicates to her employees in a call center that “customer care is the most important thing for our company.” That’s a signal to others regarding values.

(C) Now, imagine that the manager sets the incentives such that employees are paid by the number of calls they answer. This incentive sends a very different signal about what the manager is looking for: it’s about being fast, which comes at the expense of quality of care. Such mixed signals leave the employees confused about the manager’s values and expectations.

The difference in pressures on the front and back faces of the building gives rise to vortices, or spinning currents of wind, that flow downstream from the building.

To minimize building costs and maximize revenues, skyscrapers generally take the shape of squares or rectangles. These are not particularly aerodynamic shapes, and this results in a wind phenomenon called “vortex shedding.” ( ① ) As wind meets a rectangular skyscraper it pushes on the flat face of the building before flowing around its sides, where eventually it separates from the face of the structure. ( ② ) The vortices pull and push the building in a direction perpendicular to the wind at frequencies that can become dangerously self-sustaining. ( ③ ) To minimize vortex shedding, skyscraper designers do everything in their powers to confuse the wind. ( ④ ) Orienting the building so that the longer face of the structure is parallel with prevailing winds can help. ( ⑤ ) Chopping or rounding off corners of a building can likewise make it more aerodynamic. Carstensen’s (1995) socioemotional selectivity theory looks at individuals’ goals as a lifelong process that strengthens and matures with ageing. In relation to his motivational conceptual framework, Higgins (2014) proposes that motivation may even attain its highest levels in the later stages of life, subject to the balance and organisation of one’s goals in relation to life priorities. Building on this foundation, more recent research looks deeply into additional factors influencing well-being in later adulthood, particularly emphasising the role of self-worthiness, and the overall positive impact of developing a well-rounded self-view in life course transitions. Together, these studies suggest that both goal alignment and a positive self-perception are crucial for enhancing motivation and overall well-being in later life. In fact, third-age learners exhibit a higher degree of selectivity when it comes to determining which goals to pursue and how to allocate their resources towards those specific priorities. Older adults demonstrate a stronger sense of life purpose and self-fulfilment. They do it their way, and their way is an accumulation of winning and personalized combinations in effectively relating motives all together at different degrees according to their life contexts.

Many designers would argue that the most important element of lighting is visibility. Some even refer to it as the primary function of lighting. Visibility simply refers to the principle of using light to reveal or illuminate objects. In the early days, the job of the designer was nothing more than to create enough light so that the audience or occupants of a space could see. In many ways, this philosophy of lighting was based on the premise that more was better, and many believed that the more footcandles or lumens placed on a stage or in a room, the better visibility that you had. Since the 1950s or ’60s, theatrical designing moved toward a concept that we call selective visibility, which simply refers to revealing to an audience only what needs to be seen. Hence, a less-revealing image on stage might be more appropriate for the dramatic action than a fully illuminated stage. In selective visibility, areas of low intensity, shadows, silhouettes, and high contrast can become effective elements in a lighting designer’s set of tools.

Social norms are so pervasive and so deeply embedded in our performative muscle memory that we typically engage in them without even thinking. When someone greets us and asks, “How are you?,” we tend to respond automatically with something along the lines of “I’m OK” or “Not bad.” The response is hardly ever “You know, I’m having a pretty awful day, and I’m really worried because there is talk of layoffs happening at my job,” even though that may be the case. This degree of transparency upon greeting someone is typically perceived as socially awkward. The list of social norms within a given community or society is ever growing and ever changing as community members negotiate what is acceptable behavior based on the standing beliefs and ideologies of the collective. During this process, new rules are constructed and enforced to establish expectations for community members. Social norms could easily be reduced to practicing “good behavior,” but it’s much more than that. Social norms are the means by which social cohesion is achieved. And we navigate these rules, and thousands more like them, every single day.

As a general rule, when the individuals of a population encounter a new environmental stress, some individuals in the population will die prematurely and some individuals will survive. If the reason for their survival (such as a slightly enhanced ability or trait) can be passed on to their offspring (that is, it’s genetically encoded), then the next generation should be better able to withstand the newly encountered environmental stress, and the population overall will be less susceptible to it. Therefore, the key to the ability of a population to survive by adaptation lies in the   with which the next generation, the more resistant generation, is produced by the survivors of this generation. It follows that those species capable of producing a new generation very quickly should be better able to respond to a stress very quickly. Those species that require more time for reproduction will be slower to adapt to the stress because of the additional time needed for them to produce stress­tolerant offspring.

The digital age has brought remarkable advancements in communication. A message that might have taken weeks to deliver by mail can now be sent in seconds. Yet, in this shift toward efficiency, we’ve lost something essential: the richness of face­to­face interaction. Think about it — when you communicate through a text or email, you’re missing out on nonverbal cues like facial expressions, tone of voice, and body language. These elements carry emotional weight, helping us to interpret meaning and intent. Without them, our understanding of others’ emotions is often incomplete, leading to confusion and frustration. Take, for instance, a short reply to an email: “Okay.” Depending on the context, the sender’s intention might be neutral, annoyed, or even sarcastic. But without vocal inflections or facial expressions to guide us, we are left guessing. This is why digital communication requires   — not only to express ourselves effectively but also to decode the emotions behind the words we receive.

In a consumer research classic, Maloney proposed that the disbelief most people experience when encountering exaggerated product claims is often (a) overwhelmed by a natural curiosity. When advertising information (b) conflicts with existing beliefs, the resulting disagreement must be somehow resolved. This is often done by (c) yielding to the message and trying out the product in an attempt to readjust personal attitudes toward the brand. In his study, a sample of housewives was exposed to advertisements for food products and then divided into two groups: those participants that found the ad claims to be believable and the others that thought they were hard to believe. The latter group was further divided into two groups, those who confidently disbelieved the claims and those who had what Maloney described as a curious nonbelief. The latter was tied into beliefs that actual product experience was (d) unnecessary to fully judge the claims. Few consumers who clearly disbelieved the message were interested in trying the product (18%). However, Maloney’s results showed that more consumers who were in the curious nonbelief group were ready to try the product (44%) than in the group that expressed no concerns about (i.e., believed) the advertising claims (34%). The results suggest that advertising that causes consumers not to believe the message claims but makes them (e) curious may be the most effective form of new product advertising. Convincing consumers that the claims about a new product are true is not necessary to create interest in product trial.

Music allows several individuals to produce sounds together. Notably, only humans can (a) synchronize their movements (including vocalizations) flexibly in a group to an external pulse. This ability is possibly the simplest cognitive function that just separates us from animals, which would make music the (b) decisive evolutionary step of the Homo sapiens. Animals have “song” and “drumming”, but gorillas do not drum in synchrony, and whales do not sing in unison. Making music together in a group, that is, joint synchronized action, is a powerful elicitor of social bonding. Comparable to Robin Dunbar’s vocal grooming hypothesis, music might have (c) replaced manual grooming as the main mechanism for social bonding during human evolution. Dunbar’s hypothesis is based on the observation that, similar to manual grooming, human language plays a key role in building and maintaining affiliative bonds and group cohesion. This process is supposedly driven by increased group size, which (d) increases the number of social relationships an individual needs to maintain and monitor. Once the number of relationships becomes too large, an individual can no longer maintain its social networks with tactile interactions alone, and selection will favor alternative mechanisms such as talking to several individuals at the same time. However, many more individuals can make music in a group, and thus establish and foster social relationships. This makes music the more (e) unlikely candidate to maintain social networks, and increase social cohesion in large groups. Thus a musical grooming hypothesis seems at least as likely to explain the emergence of music as a vocal grooming hypothesis for the emergence of language.

1In his study, a sample of housewives was exposed to advertisements for food products and then divided into two groups: those participants that found the ad claims to be believable and the others that thought they were hard to believe.
그의 연구에서 표본으로 선정된 주부들은 식품 광고에 노출된 다음, 두 집단, 즉 광고의 주장을 믿을 만하다고 여긴 참가자들과 그것을 믿기 어렵다고 생각한 나머지 참가자들로 나뉘었다.
2The latter group was further divided into two groups, those who confidently disbelieved the claims and those who had what Maloney described as a curious nonbelief.
후자의 집단은 더 나아가 두 집단, 즉 확신을 갖고 그 주장을 불신한 사람들과 Maloney가 ‘호기심 어린 불신’이라고 묘사한 것을 지닌 사람들로 나뉘었다.
3Few consumers who clearly disbelieved the message were interested in trying the product (18%).
메시지를 분명히 불신했던 소비자 중 제품을 사용해 보는 데 관심이 있었던 사람은 거의 없었다(18퍼센트).
4However, Maloney’s results showed that more consumers who were in the curious nonbelief group were ready to try the product (44%) than in the group that expressed no concerns about (i.e., believed) the advertising claims (34%).
그러나 Maloney의 결과는 호기심 어린 불신 집단에 있던 소비자들이 그 광고 주장에 대해 아무런 우려를 표하지 않은(즉, 그것을 믿은) 집단보다(34퍼센트) 더 많이(44퍼센트) 제품을 써 볼 준비가 되어 있었다는 것을 보여 주었다.
5Convincing consumers that the claims about a new product are true is not necessary to create interest in product trial.
제품을 사용해 보는 데 관심을 갖게 하기 위해 신제품에 관한 주장이 사실이라고 소비자들을 납득시킬 필요는 없다.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

비교는 형태와 비교 대상, 시제는 시간 표현을 먼저 본다.

01원급 비교 — as ~ as

「A as 원급 as B」는 A와 B가 같은 정도. 부정은 not as(so) ~ as, 배수는 배수사 + as ~ as.

형태뜻
as 원급 as~만큼 …한
not as(so) 원급 as~만큼 …하지 않은
three times as 원급 as~의 세 배만큼 …한
not so much A as B 심화A라기보다는 B
원급Coastal wind turbines now generate power nearly as efficiently as offshore ones, yet their maintenance costs substantially less.
배수Respondents in the survey checked their phones three times as often as they had a decade earlier, usually without being aware of it.

주의as와 as 사이에는 원급만, 배수사는 첫 as 앞: as three times large as (×)

02비교급 + than — 비교 대상을 맞춘다

비교하는 두 대상은 같은 종류여야 한다. 반복되는 명사는 that(단수) / those(복수)로 받는다.

thatThe average income of rural households remains far lower than that of urban households, despite generous government support.
thoseThe side effects reported by patients who received the new drug were milder than those reported by patients in the placebo group.

학평·수능than 뒤 that / those 고르기 — 수식어를 걷어 내고 앞 명사의 수를 확인한다.

03비교급 · 최상급 강조 — 「훨씬」 · 「단연」

비교급 앞 「훨씬」은 much · even · far · still · a lot. very는 원급만 꾸민다. 최상급은 by far · much로 강조.

muchElectric vehicles produce much less pollution than gasoline cars, although manufacturing their batteries consumes immense energy.
by farThe Amazon is by far the largest tropical rainforest on Earth, covering a vast terrain across nine countries.

주의very more (×) · very better (×) — by far는 최상급 앞, very는 최상급 뒤(the very best)

04the 비교급, the 비교급 — ~할수록 더 …하다

the 비교급 + S + V, the 비교급 + S + V. 「비교급 and 비교급」은 「점점 더 ~」.

The more carefully engineers test → the fewer repairs it needs
the 비교급The more carefully engineers test a bridge before it opens, the fewer structural repairs it will need during its first decades of use.
점점As global temperatures kept rising, summers grew hotter and hotter, forcing farmers to abandon crops that required abundant precipitation.

학평·수능the 비교급 뒤 어순(the more carefully engineers test)과 형용사/부사 자리를 묻는다.

강의 40분

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

조동사는 말하는 사람의 확신 · 후회 · 의무를, 가정법은 사실과 반대인 상상을 나타낸다. 고3 지문에서는 시점 단서(last year · now)가 삽입구 너머에 숨어 있다.

01추측의 조동사 — must · may · can’t

핵심강한 추측 must(~임에 틀림없다), 약한 추측 may / might(~일지도 모른다), 강한 부정 추측 can’t(~일 리 없다).

mustGiven how carefully the male bowerbird arranges every shell and stone by size, the display must serve a purpose far beyond simple decoration.
can’tThe two manuscripts, which differ in both handwriting and vocabulary, can’t be the work of a single author, however similar their plots may seem to a casual reader.

주의「~일 리 없다」는 mustn’t가 아니라 can’t. mustn’t는 「~하면 안 된다」(금지).

02조동사 + have p.p. — 과거에 대한 추측 · 후회

핵심지나간 일을 지금 추측하거나 후회할 때는 조동사 뒤에 have p.p.를 쓴다.

형태뜻
must have p.p.~했음에 틀림없다
may(might) have p.p.~했을지도 모른다
can’t have p.p.~했을 리 없다
should have p.p.~했어야 했는데 (안 했다)
need not have p.p.~할 필요가 없었는데 (했다)
could have p.p.~할 수도 있었는데 (안 했다) 심화
추측The notebook’s earliest pages contain no equations, so the mathematician must have developed her notation much later.
후회The commission should have consulted local ecologists before it drained the wetlands, since several species that once thrived there have now vanished, and the surviving populations continue to dwindle.

학평·수능last year · in 1990처럼 과거 표현이 있으면 「조동사 + 동사원형」이 아니라 「조동사 + have p.p.」

03요구 · 제안 + that + S + (should) 동사원형

핵심insist · demand · suggest · recommend · require 뒤 that절이 「해야 한다」는 내용이면 (should) 동사원형. 심화 It is essential · vital · necessary that 뒤도 같다.

요구The editor demanded that every chapter of the biography be verified against the original letters before the book went to print.
심화It is essential that a mentor not simply give advice but also listen closely to the concerns of the employees he or she supports.

주의that절이 「사실」이면 시제 일치: The data suggested that males with larger displays attracted more females.

04used to · would · be used to -ing

핵심과거의 습관·상태는 used to(상태 O), 과거의 반복 동작은 would(상태 X), 「~에 익숙하다」는 be used to -ing.

상태There used to be vast wetlands across northern England before large areas were drained and planted with fast-growing foreign trees.
동작As a young teacher, she would collect her students’ drafts every Friday and return them with detailed comments.

주의would는 상태(be · live · have)에 못 쓴다. 심화 be used to + 동사원형은 「~하는 데 쓰이다」: Lotteries were used to select officials in ancient Athens.

05had better · would rather · may as well

핵심뒤에는 모두 동사원형. 부정은 had better not · would rather not.

충고Writers who receive harsh feedback had better not abandon their drafts, since most strong essays emerge only after several rounds of revision.
선택Critics who are skeptical of empathy would rather rely on rational compassion than trust emotions that tend to favor members of their own group, especially during intense competition.

주의had not better (×) → had better not (○) / would rather A than B에서 A · B는 같은 동사원형.

06가정법 과거 — 지금 사실과 반대

핵심If + S + 과거형(be는 were), S + would / could + 동사원형. 해석은 「(지금) ~라면 …할 텐데」.

현재If leaves stayed on the branches all winter, strong winds would damage the tree, and it would lose more water than its frozen roots could absorb.
wereIf officials were chosen entirely by lottery, voters would have little reason to study the candidates’ policies.

학평·수능주절에 would + 동사원형이 보이면 if절은 과거형. 단순 조건(If it rains, …)과 구별.

07가정법 과거완료 — 과거 사실과 반대

핵심If + S + had p.p., S + would / could + have p.p. 해석은 「(그때) ~했더라면 …했을 텐데」.

과거If the historians had not found the builder’s bills in the archive, they would never have known how much the cathedral actually cost.
couldIf the forest managers had listened to ecologists earlier, they could have protected several rare species that disappeared once the wetlands were drained and replaced with plantations of imported trees.

주의if절에 would를 쓰지 않는다: If they would have listened (×)

08혼합 가정법 — 과거 일이 지금에 영향

핵심If + S + had p.p.(과거), S + would + 동사원형(지금). 주절의 now · today · still이 단서.

혼합If a single author had not created Sherlock Holmes, the fictional detective’s personality would probably be far less consistent across the stories we read today.
혼합If the town had protected its wetlands decades ago, the region would now support far greater biodiversity.

학평·수능앞은 과거 표현, 뒤는 now · today — 시점이 다르면 혼합 가정법.

09I wish · as if · Without

핵심I wish / as if + 과거형 = 같은 때 사실의 반대, + had p.p. = 그 이전 사실의 반대. 심화 Without(But for) ~ = If it were not for(지금) / If it had not been for(과거).

wishMany students wish they had received feedback on their early drafts rather than a single grade after the essay was finished.
as ifThe male stands at the end of the avenue as if he were larger than he actually is, relying on the intricate illusion he has built.
WithoutWithout the surviving letters, diaries, and court chronicles, historians would know almost nothing about the daily lives of the thousands of workers who built the palace over three decades.

주의I wish 뒤 현재형은 쓰지 않는다: I wish I have more time (×) → had

10If 생략 도치 — Were · Had · Should

핵심If를 빼면 동사가 주어 앞으로 간다: If I were → Were I / If he had known → Had he known / If you should need → Should you need.

원래If 생략
If I were you, …Were I you, …
If she had known, …Had she known, …
If you should have questions, …Should you have questions, …
HadHad the critics examined the data more closely, they would have noticed that empathy reduced conflict in some of the groups studied.
ShouldShould any participant feel uncomfortable, he or she may withdraw from the study without penalty.

학평·수능「Had + S + p.p.」로 시작하면 주절은 would have p.p. — 문장 첫 단어를 보고 판단.

When gathering the preferences of multiple agents into one collective choice, it is easily seen that certain cases call for                       . For example, if there are two alternatives, a and b, and two agents such that one prefers a and the other one b, there is no deterministic way of selecting a single alternative without violating one of two basic fairness conditions known as anonymity and neutrality. Anonymity requires that the collective choice ought to be independent of the agents’ identities whereas neutrality requires impartiality towards the alternatives. Allowing lotteries as social outcomes hence seems like a necessity for impartial collective choice. Indeed, most common “deterministic” social choice functions such as plurality rule are only deterministic as long as there is no tie, which is usually resolved by drawing a lot.
